Each week has a problem focus, the official syllabus topic, the software tools involved, and an AI-aware validation task.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start with the workload guide

The website is a complete resource bank, not a list of tasks that are all due.
The [weekly workload guide](workload-guide.qmd) identifies core exercises,
guided practice, extension work, and the role of each lab.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Launch block and roadmap

Weeks 1-4 are ready for the start of the semester. Weeks 5-15 show the planned
direction of the course and may be refined after the class has worked through
the opening block. For assigned work and dates, use the current week and the
latest Blackboard announcement.
:::

## Course Roadmap

Every week includes:

- a two-meeting teaching plan;
- a detailed MATLAB or R lab;
- an AI code critique activity;
- a student exercise set;
- multiple starter scripts.

The [workload guide](workload-guide.qmd) defines the default student selection.

## Phase Recovery Checkpoints

These optional pages collect the minimum knowledge needed before a transition.
They are not additional assignments unless announced in class.

- [After Week 5: ready for R](recovery-after-week-05.qmd)
- [After Week 10: ready for reusable R workflows](recovery-after-week-10.qmd)
- [After Week 12: ready for modeling](recovery-after-week-12.qmd)

## Weekly Pattern

Each week follows the same rhythm:

1. Start from a mathematical or statistical question.
2. Build a small computational workflow.
3. Use MATLAB or R to produce output.
4. Check the output against expectations.
5. Critique any AI-generated code or explanation.
6. Save work in a reproducible form.
